source.title: Deep Learning on a Data Diet: Finding Important Examples Early in Training
source.authors: Mansheej Paul; S. Ganguli; G. Dziugaite

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied. It notes that this v2 corrects erroneous GraNd-at-initialization results caused by a Flax bug.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training and data-pruning outcomes, but does not test whether the listed claim versions hold. Its training-error-barrier measure concerns connectivity between trajectories, not whether training reaches zero or near-zero classification error; the paper does not report the claim versions' training-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The study trains ResNets and VGG13 on data subsets, but reports test accuracy and error barriers rather than the training classification-error results named by the claim versions. GraNd/EL2N scores and pruning results are not evidence that the stated training-error claims hold.
record.test_reason: The study reports data-pruning test accuracy, example scores, NTK evolution and linear mode connectivity, rather than outcomes testing V1–V6. In particular, a near-zero training error barrier measures connectivity between trajectories, not near-zero training classification error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: early averaged GraNd and EL2N scores identify useful training subsets; higher-scoring examples are associated with faster NTK evolution and more persistent error barriers; excluding the very highest scores can help depending on noise and pruning level. These observations do not establish any of V1–V6.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates data-example scoring and dataset pruning, not the training-error interventions or measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that pruning outcomes vary with score-computation time, pruning fraction, score averaging across runs, dataset, and label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Early EL2N-based pruning preserves test accuracy across substantial pruning ranges on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and CINIC-10; extreme pruning harms performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early example scores identify subsets that preserve generalization, with effectiveness depending on pruning level.

fits_no_version.finding: Excluding the highest-scoring examples improves test accuracy in some sliding-window settings, especially with label corruption; clean CIFAR-10 shows no such boost at 50% pruning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of excluding the hardest examples depends on label noise and retained dataset size.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher EL2N-score subsets generally have greater NTK velocity, with a sharp decline for the highest scores under label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Example difficulty relates to feature evolution during training, with a qualification for noisy examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Training error barriers approach zero earlier on low-score subsets than on high-score subsets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear mode connectivity develops earlier on easier training examples.

record.problems: The main pruning and dynamics findings are primarily plotted, with means and 16th-to-84th percentile shading across four runs; no training classification-error results relevant to the supplied versions are reported. The text documents an earlier GraNd-at-initialization bug and correction in this version.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: reported outcomes concern test accuracy, score correlations, kernel velocity, and training error barriers, none of which directly measures the behaviors specified by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether training classification error reaches zero or near-zero on clean or corrupted CIFAR labels, and its dependence on capacity or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of initialization schemes on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth. Averaging example scores across initializations does not test these effects.
Loss and curvature dynamics around learning-rate stability thresholds. The hyperparameter search does not report these dynamics.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation should change from tests to discusses; T6 is appropriate. Figures 10–11 contain conflicting caption language about training accuracy, but their axes and comparison descriptions identify test accuracy, so they do not supply V1 results. The corrected v2 explicitly withdraws the earlier successful GraNd-at-initialization finding; the discussion retains inconsistent language suggesting success at initialization.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report whether models achieve zero or near-zero training classification error on the full or corrupted-label datasets, or compare that outcome across model sizes, optimizers, stopping times, and regularization.
No two-layer teacher-student experiment, neuron-width sweep, or frequency of spurious-minimum outcomes is reported.
No comparison of plain and residual networks' training classification error across depth is reported.
The paper does not compare initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth.
The paper does not vary learning rates around a stability threshold or report the described loss and curvature dynamics.
The paper does not compare batch-normalized and unnormalized models for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The paper discusses related optimization dynamics but reports no results testing the claim versions. A near-zero training error barrier measures connectivity between trajectories, not near-zero training classification error.

tranche.reason: The study measures data-pruning test accuracy, example importance, NTK evolution and linear mode connectivity. These outcomes neither test V1–V6 nor use those findings as a tool.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is the March 2023 revision correcting erroneous GraNd-at-initialization results caused by a Flax bug. Its discussion retains an initialization-pruning claim inconsistent with the corrected results in Section 3.
